dimensions.note: The model handles no secrets. It runs go, git and just locally and writes files; it makes no authenticated call and reads no vault. The one personal value it touches is the Code of Conduct contact address, which is published in the generated repository by design and is not a credential.

All four methods log at info on entry and on completion, with structured placeholders throughout — context.logger.info('Wrote {written}, overwrote {overwritten}, skipped {skipped}', {...}). No string interpolation into messages. Nothing sensitive is logged; the email argument never reaches a log line.

Errors throw before any write. The withCodeOfConduct/email guard runs before varsFor and before the write loop, so a misconfigured run leaves no partial project. runCommand includes the command, its arguments, the exit code and both output streams. render throws naming the unknown variable rather than emitting a hole into a generated file. No broad catch swallows anything: the one catch is a two-line Deno.lstat existence probe.

28 tests cover the pure functions — render, planFor, badgesFor, varsFor, the schema, and the coupling between workflows and the configs they read. They found a real defect on their first run: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md was in the plan twice and ungated. But execute() itself is untested, because it needs extensionFile and createModelTestContext does not provide it. The gap is real and known: the schema-write violation fixed during this review lived in execute and no test would have caught it.

write_files skips an existing file unless overwrite is on, and overwrite reaches generated files only, never the seeded ones a project has since written. create_project is idempotent: mkdir is recursive and git init on an existing repository is a no-op. Partial failure leaves partially written files, which is acceptable here because a re-run completes rather than conflicts — the operation is file creation in a directory the user named, not a remote resource that could orphan.

No HTTP call, no external API, no pagination. The only network access in anything this produces is the generated justfile's curl of shared recipes, which runs in the generated project rather than in this model.

No sockets, handles or temporary files. File access is Deno.readTextFile and Deno.writeTextFile, which manage their own handles. Deno.Command output is fully buffered and consumed. Nothing is created that would need later cleanup — the model's only durable effect is the project directory the caller asked for.

Fixed during development, and the reason this dimension matters here. CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md shipped john@dewey.ws in its enforcement section, copied verbatim, so every consumer would have published a code of conduct naming a stranger as the person to report harassment to; it takes @@email@@ now and write_files refuses to run without one. AI_POLICY.md named osapi-io in four places and is generic. No IP addresses, hostnames, subnets or account identifiers anywhere. One real URL remains by design: justfilesRepo defaults to the osapi-io justfiles, used only when sharedJustfiles is explicitly turned on, which is off by default.
GlobalArgsSchema and StateSchema are both plain z.object with no .passthrough(). Every field is typed, and projectName carries a regex rejecting anything Go cannot use as a module or package name.

The one resource spec, state, declares lifetime 'infinite' and garbageCollection 10. Infinite is right because the record of what a scaffolder wrote is the audit trail for a directory that still exists; 10 versions bounds it.

Not a CRUD lifecycle model. It scaffolds a directory once and optionally re-renders it; there is no remote resource to update, delete or sync. The four methods are stages of one operation, chained by the workflows' dependsOn.

The mutating methods carry no labelled pre-flight checks. check_prereqs is effectively one — it verifies go, git and just before anything is created — but it is a separate method rather than a labelled check on create_project and write_files, so it cannot be selectively skipped and nothing stops someone running write_files alone. That is exactly what the retemplate workflow does deliberately, so the shape is intentional, but the labels are missing.

One spec, one instance name, 'current', written by all four methods with the same schema shape. No collision is possible. Verified mechanically: all four writeResource calls match StateSchema field for field.

Fixed during this review, by its mechanical schema-write check. check_prereqs, create_project and bootstrap each hardcoded filesWritten, filesSkipped and filesOverwritten to [], so running bootstrap after write_files erased the record of what had just been written. They read the prior state forward through readResource now, via a priorFileLists helper. No direct dataRepository access anywhere.
First version. Nothing published to upgrade from, and no migration to declare.
